title: A Green Cloud in the Sea, Seen From Space
summary: A satellite took a photo of something strange in the sea near Canada. Under the water, there was a giant green cloud about 4 miles long. The cloud is made of milt. Milt is a fluid with sperm that male fish let out to fertilize eggs. It came from Pacific herring, a kind of fish. The fish gather in big groups to have babies. The females lay eggs on kelp and rocks. Then the males let out milt over the eggs. The milt is really white, not green. It looks green because it is close to the surface of the water. The photo was taken on February 19, 2026, by a satellite called Landsat 9. It shows Barkley Sound, near Vancouver Island in Canada. This place is perfect for herring. The water is calm, the bottom is rocky, and the salt is low. The cloud stayed for about 48 hours. Herring are important food for salmon and for many other animals. During the event, whales, sea lions, eagles, wolves and bears come to eat the herring.
why_it_matters: Fish like herring feed salmon, whales and people, so watching them helps us protect the sea.
